name: Lemon
description: Yellow citrus fruit with sharp, acidic juice and a fragrant, oily peel. Used for juice, twists, wheels and wedges in most sour style drinks.

name: Lime
description: Small green citrus with tart, slightly bitter juice and aromatic peel. The standard acid for Daiquiris, Margaritas and most tropical drinks.

name: Orange
description: Sweet citrus fruit with mild acidity and an oil-rich peel. Used for juice, wedges and twists, and the peel is a common aromatic garnish.

name: Blood Orange
description: Orange variety with deep red flesh and a berry-like, slightly bitter flavour. In season through winter and used for juice, wheels and syrups.

name: Grapefruit
description: Large citrus fruit with bittersweet, tart juice and a thick aromatic peel. Used for juice, wedges and long twists in drinks like the Paloma.

name: Pink Grapefruit
description: Grapefruit with pink to red flesh that is sweeter and less bitter than white varieties. The usual choice for juicing and garnishing behind the bar.

name: Mandarin
description: Small, easy-peeling citrus with sweet, low-acid juice and a floral peel. Used for juice, oleo saccharum and peel garnishes when in season.

name: Yuzu
description: East Asian citrus with a highly aromatic peel and tart juice that tastes between lemon, mandarin and grapefruit. Fresh fruit is seasonal and scarce.

name: Bergamot
description: Sour citrus grown mainly in Calabria, known for the floral, perfumed oil in its peel. The scent of Earl Grey tea, used for peel, juice and cordials.

name: Calamansi
description: Small round citrus from the Philippines and Southeast Asia with very sour juice and a sweet, thin peel. Tastes like a cross of lime and mandarin.

name: Finger Lime
description: Australian native citrus shaped like a small finger, filled with tiny juice beads that pop like caviar. Used as a tart garnish on top of drinks.

name: Makrut Lime
description: Knobbly green citrus from Southeast Asia, also called kaffir lime. The fruit has little juice, so the intensely fragrant zest is the part that gets used.

name: Kumquat
description: Tiny oval citrus eaten whole, with a sweet edible skin and sour flesh. Muddled into drinks, candied for garnish or cooked into syrups and marmalade.

name: Lemon Juice
description: Juice pressed from fresh lemons, around 6 percent acid. The main souring agent in Whiskey Sours, Collinses and most gin and brandy sours.

name: Lime Juice
description: Juice pressed from fresh limes, tart with a faint bitterness. It is the acid in Daiquiris, Margaritas, Gimlets and Mojitos and is best used the day it is squeezed.

name: Orange Juice
description: Juice pressed from sweet oranges, low in acid and high in sugar. Poured in the Mimosa, Screwdriver and Blood and Sand, and often paired with lemon for balance.

name: Blood Orange Juice
description: Red juice pressed from blood oranges, with berry notes and a little more bitterness than regular orange juice. Seasonal when fresh, also sold chilled.

name: Grapefruit Juice
description: Juice pressed from grapefruit, bittersweet and moderately tart. Used in the Paloma, Hemingway Daiquiri, Greyhound and Brown Derby.

name: Pink Grapefruit Juice
description: Juice from pink or ruby grapefruit, sweeter and softer in bitterness than juice from white grapefruit. The common choice for Palomas and spritzes.

name: Pineapple Juice
description: Juice from ripe pineapple, sweet and tangy, and it foams well when shaken. A core ingredient in the Piña Colada, Jungle Bird and many tiki drinks.

name: Cranberry Juice
description: Tart red juice from cranberries, usually sold sweetened as cranberry juice drink. Poured in the Cosmopolitan, Sea Breeze and Cape Codder.

name: Apple Juice
description: Juice pressed from apples, either clear or cloudy. Cloudy pressed juice gives a fresher apple flavour and is the usual pick for long drinks and highballs.

name: Passion Fruit Juice
description: Strained juice from passion fruit pulp, very tart and strongly tropical. Used in the Hurricane and Pornstar Martini, fresh or from a carton or frozen pack.

name: Yuzu Juice
description: Tart, fragrant juice of the yuzu citrus, usually bought bottled from Japan or Korea. A small measure adds a floral lemon and mandarin note to sours.

name: Pomegranate Juice
description: Deep red juice pressed from pomegranate seeds, sweet, tart and a little tannic. It is the base for real grenadine and is also poured on its own in long drinks.

name: Watermelon Juice
description: Light, sweet juice blended and strained from watermelon flesh. Low in acid, so it is normally paired with lime in summer coolers and Margaritas.

name: Carrot Juice
description: Sweet, earthy orange juice pressed from carrots. Used in savoury and brunch style drinks, often alongside ginger, citrus or aquavit.

name: Beetroot Juice
description: Deep purple juice pressed from beetroot, sweet and earthy. A small amount gives strong colour, so it is used for both flavour and a vivid red hue.

name: Cucumber Juice
description: Pale green juice pressed from fresh cucumber, cool and lightly vegetal. Used in gin and tequila coolers and needs to be made fresh as it fades quickly.

name: Ginger Juice
description: Hot, pungent juice pressed from fresh ginger root. Used in small amounts for heat or mixed with sugar to make ginger syrup for Penicillins and Mules.

name: Mango Juice
description: Thick, sweet juice or nectar made from ripe mango. Usually bought in cartons and used in tropical long drinks, often cut with lime for acidity.

name: Guava Juice
description: Thick pink juice or nectar made from guava, sweet with a musky tropical aroma. Common in tiki and Latin American style drinks, normally bought in cartons.

name: Lychee Juice
description: Sweet, floral juice made from lychee, usually sold in cartons or taken from the tinned fruit. The base of the Lychee Martini and similar drinks.

name: Coconut Water
description: The clear liquid inside young green coconuts, lightly sweet, nutty and a little salty. Used as a lengthener and for dilution in stirred and tropical drinks.

name: Pineapple
description: Tropical fruit with sweet, tangy yellow flesh. Juiced, muddled, grilled or cut into wedges, and the fronds are a common tiki garnish.

name: Passion Fruit
description: Round tropical fruit with a wrinkled purple or yellow shell and tart, seedy, aromatic pulp. Halves are floated as garnish and the pulp goes into shaken drinks.

name: Strawberry
description: Soft red berry with a sweet, fragrant flavour and gentle acidity. Muddled fresh, cooked into syrups and shrubs, or sliced as a garnish.

name: Raspberry
description: Small red berry, tart and perfumed. Muddled in drinks like the Clover Club, cooked into syrup, or skewered fresh as a garnish.

name: Blackberry
description: Dark purple berry with a sweet, tart and slightly earthy flavour. Muddled or used as the garnish on a Bramble, and cooked into syrups and liqueurs.

name: Blueberry
description: Small blue berry with a mild, sweet flavour and low acidity. Muddled, cooked into syrups and shrubs, or threaded on a pick as a garnish.

name: Cherry
description: Fresh stone fruit with sweet or sour red flesh, in season through summer. Muddled, cooked into syrups, or preserved to make cocktail cherries.

name: Peach
description: Soft stone fruit with sweet, fragrant flesh and a fuzzy skin. Puréed for the Bellini, muddled into smashes, or sliced as a garnish in summer.

name: Apricot
description: Small orange stone fruit, sweet with a tart edge and an almond-like note near the stone. Used fresh, dried or as jam in syrups and shaken drinks.

name: Mango
description: Tropical stone fruit with sweet, rich orange flesh. Blended into purée, cooked into syrups or cut into cheeks and slices for garnish.

name: Banana
description: Soft, sweet tropical fruit. Blended into frozen drinks, cooked into syrups, infused into rum, or dried into chips for garnish. The peel is used in cordials too.

name: Watermelon
description: Large melon with crisp, watery red flesh and a light, sweet flavour. Juiced or muddled for summer drinks, and cut into wedges for garnish.

name: Melon
description: Sweet, juicy fruit such as honeydew, rockmelon or Galia. Juiced, blended or balled for garnish, with a soft flavour that suits gin, sake and sherry.

name: Honeydew Melon
description: Smooth-skinned melon with pale green flesh and a clean, sugary flavour. Juiced for cordials and coolers or cut into balls and slices as a garnish.

name: Apple
description: Crisp fruit ranging from sweet to tart depending on the variety. Juiced, cooked into syrups, or sliced into fans as a garnish.

name: Green Apple
description: Tart, crisp apple such as Granny Smith with bright green skin. Juiced for its sharp flavour and colour, or sliced thin for garnish.

name: Pear
description: Soft, juicy fruit with a mild, floral sweetness and a grainy texture. Puréed, juiced or poached for syrups, and sliced as a garnish in autumn drinks.

name: Fig
description: Soft fruit with purple or green skin and sweet, jammy, seeded flesh. Muddled, cooked into syrups and jams, or halved as a garnish in late summer.

name: Lychee
description: Small fruit with rough red skin and translucent white flesh that tastes sweet and floral. Used fresh or tinned, muddled or skewered as a garnish.

name: Guava
description: Tropical fruit with pink or white flesh, a musky aroma and a sweet, slightly tart taste. Usually used as purée, juice or syrup in tropical drinks.

name: Coconut
description: Fruit of the coconut palm, with firm white flesh and clear water inside. The flesh is grated, toasted or pressed for milk and cream, and the shell can serve drinks.

name: Pomegranate
description: Fruit with a leathery red skin packed with juicy, tart red seeds. The seeds are pressed for juice and grenadine or scattered over drinks as a garnish.

name: Rhubarb
description: Pink and green stalks with a sharp, sour taste, used as a fruit once cooked with sugar. Made into syrups, cordials and shrubs in spring.

name: Kiwi
description: Small brown fuzzy fruit with bright green flesh, tiny black seeds and a sweet, tangy flavour. Muddled or juiced, and sliced into wheels for garnish.

name: Plum
description: Stone fruit with smooth skin and juicy flesh that runs from sweet to tart. Cooked into syrups and shrubs, muddled fresh or sliced for garnish.

name: Grape
description: Small juicy fruit grown in bunches, green, red or black. Muddled in smashes, frozen to chill a drink without dilution, or skewered as a garnish.

name: Cranberry
description: Small, firm red berry that is very tart and slightly bitter when raw. Cooked into syrups and shrubs or floated fresh as a winter garnish.

name: Blackcurrant
description: Small dark purple berry with a sharp, tannic and deeply fruity flavour. The fruit behind crème de cassis, also cooked into syrups and cordials.

name: Papaya
description: Tropical fruit with soft orange flesh and a mild, musky sweetness. Blended into purées and cordials, while green papaya is used for savoury pickles.

name: Soursop
description: Large spiky green tropical fruit with creamy white pulp. It tastes like a mix of pineapple, strawberry and citrus and is used as juice or purée.

name: Tamarind
description: Brown pod fruit with sticky, sweet and sour pulp. Sold as pods, blocks or paste and made into syrups and sodas, common in Mexican and Thai style drinks.

name: Winter Melon
description: Large pale gourd, also called wax gourd, with very mild white flesh. In East Asia it is cooked with sugar into a caramel-like syrup and tea.

name: Aloe Vera
description: Succulent plant whose leaves hold a clear, mild gel. The gel or bottled aloe juice adds a fresh, green and slightly bitter note and a soft texture.

name: Cucumber
description: Cool, watery green vegetable with a fresh, mild flavour. Muddled or juiced in gin and tequila drinks, and cut into ribbons, slices or spears for garnish.

name: Tomato
description: Red savoury fruit with sweet, acidic and umami-rich flesh. Juiced for Bloody Marys, strained into clear tomato water, or used fresh as a garnish.

name: Cherry Tomato
description: Small, sweet tomato about the size of a grape. Muddled into savoury drinks, pickled, or skewered whole as a garnish for Bloody Marys and Martinis.

name: Almond
description: Mild, sweet tree nut and the base of orgeat syrup. Used blanched or toasted for syrups, milks and infusions, or grated over a drink.

name: Hazelnut
description: Round brown nut with a sweet, toasty flavour once roasted. Made into syrups, orgeat style milks and infusions, and pairs well with coffee and chocolate.

name: Pistachio
description: Green nut with a rich, slightly sweet and resinous flavour. Used for pistachio orgeat and syrups, or crushed as a rim or garnish.

name: Walnut
description: Wrinkled tree nut with an earthy, slightly bitter and tannic flavour. Toasted for syrups and infusions, and green walnuts are used to make nocino.

name: Peanut
description: Legume eaten as a nut, with a rich, savoury flavour when roasted. Used for fat washing spirits, in orgeat style syrups, or salted as a bar snack garnish.

name: Macadamia
description: Australian native nut with a buttery, mild and slightly sweet flavour. Toasted and made into orgeat, syrups and nut milks, or used to fat wash spirits.

name: Peanut Butter
description: Smooth or crunchy paste of ground roasted peanuts. Used to fat wash bourbon and rum or blended into syrups for a nutty, salty note.

name: Mint
description: Fresh green herb with a cool, sweet menthol flavour, usually spearmint. Essential for the Mojito, Mint Julep and Southside, and the default sprig garnish.

name: Basil
description: Soft green herb with a sweet, peppery, clove-like aroma. Muddled or shaken into drinks like the Gin Basil Smash, or used as a leaf garnish.

name: Thai Basil
description: Basil variety with purple stems and a spicy, anise-like flavour. Holds up well when shaken and suits gin, rum and tequila with lime.

name: Micro Purple Basil
description: Tiny young leaves of purple basil, picked a couple of weeks after sprouting. Placed on foam or ice as a delicate garnish with a mild basil flavour.

name: Rosemary
description: Woody herb with needle-like leaves and a piney, resinous aroma. Used as a sprig garnish, lightly torched for smoke, or steeped into syrups.

name: Thyme
description: Small-leaved woody herb with an earthy, slightly floral and savoury aroma. Steeped into syrups and honey or used as a sprig garnish.

name: Sage
description: Soft grey-green herb with a savoury, slightly peppery and camphor-like aroma. Muddled, steeped into syrups, or used as a single leaf garnish.

name: Coriander
description: Leafy green herb, called cilantro in the US, with a bright citrus and green flavour. Muddled or shaken into tequila and gin drinks with lime.

name: Dill
description: Feathery green herb with a grassy, anise-like flavour. Pairs with aquavit, gin and cucumber, and is used in savoury drinks, brines and as a frond garnish.

name: Tarragon
description: Slender-leaved herb with a sweet anise and liquorice flavour. Muddled or steeped into syrups and works well with gin, citrus and stone fruit.

name: Parsley
description: Bright green herb with a clean, grassy and lightly peppery flavour. Used in savoury and green juice style drinks, herb oils and as a garnish.

name: Oregano
description: Mediterranean herb with a warm, savoury and slightly bitter aroma. Used fresh or dried in tinctures, syrups and savoury drinks with tomato or olive.

name: Shiso
description: Japanese herb with broad, serrated leaves and a flavour between mint, basil and anise. Shaken into drinks, steeped into syrups or used as a leaf garnish.

name: Lemongrass
description: Tall fibrous grass with a lemony, floral aroma and no acidity. Bruised and steeped into syrups and infusions, or trimmed into a stirrer garnish.

name: Makrut Lime Leaf
description: Glossy double-lobed leaf of the makrut lime, with a strong floral citrus aroma. Steeped into syrups and spirits or floated as a garnish.

name: Curry Leaf
description: Small glossy leaf from South Asia with a nutty, citrusy and savoury aroma. Fried or steeped into syrups and spirits, or used fresh as a garnish.

name: Pandan
description: Long green leaf from Southeast Asia with a sweet, grassy aroma often compared to vanilla and toasted rice. Steeped into syrups or tied as a garnish.

name: Bay Leaf
description: Stiff, aromatic leaf of the bay laurel with a herbal, slightly floral and peppery scent. Steeped into syrups and tinctures or used as a garnish.

name: Lemon Verbena
description: Shrub with long, rough leaves that give off a strong, sweet lemon scent. Used fresh or dried in syrups, teas and infusions, or as a leaf garnish.

name: Lemon Myrtle
description: Australian native tree whose leaves carry an intense lemon and lemongrass aroma. Used fresh or dried in syrups, teas, cordials and gin infusions.

name: Fennel
description: Pale bulb vegetable with feathery fronds and a sweet anise flavour. The bulb is juiced or steeped into syrups and the fronds are used as a garnish.

name: Eucalyptus
description: Leaves of the Australian gum tree, with a cooling, camphor and menthol aroma. Used sparingly in tinctures, syrups and smoke, or as a leaf garnish.

name: Fig Leaf
description: Large leaf of the fig tree with a green, coconut and vanilla-like aroma once toasted or steeped. Used for syrups, oils, infusions and as a coaster garnish.

name: Lavender
description: Purple flower buds with a strong floral, slightly soapy and herbal aroma. Used dried in syrups, bitters and honey, or fresh as a sprig garnish.

name: Elderflower
description: Creamy white flower heads of the elder tree, with a sweet, floral and lychee-like scent. Steeped into cordial in late spring, or used dried.

name: Hibiscus
description: Dried red calyces of the roselle plant, tart and cranberry-like with a deep crimson colour. Steeped into teas, syrups and agua de Jamaica.

name: Rose
description: Fragrant petals of the rose, used fresh or dried. Steeped into syrups and teas or scattered as a garnish, giving a sweet, perfumed floral note.

name: Jasmine
description: Small white flowers with a heady, sweet floral perfume. Most often used dried or as jasmine scented tea, steeped into syrups and cordials.

name: Chamomile
description: Small daisy-like flowers, dried for their apple, honey and hay aroma. Steeped into syrups, teas and infusions, and pairs with whisky, gin and honey.

name: Osmanthus
description: Tiny golden flowers from East Asia with an apricot and peach-like fragrance. Sold dried and steeped into teas, syrups, honey and wine.

name: Chrysanthemum
description: Dried yellow or white flower heads with a mild, honeyed and slightly bitter herbal flavour. Steeped as a tea or into syrups, common in East Asian drinks.

name: Cinnamon
description: Warm, sweet spice from the inner bark of cinnamon trees. Steeped into syrups for tiki drinks, or grated and dusted over the top of a drink.

name: Cinnamon Stick
description: Rolled quill of dried cinnamon bark. Used whole as a garnish or stirrer in hot and tiki drinks, sometimes lit for smoke, and simmered into syrup.

name: Nutmeg
description: Hard brown seed with a warm, sweet and woody spice flavour. Grated fresh over flips, eggnog and punches as a finishing garnish.

name: Clove
description: Dried flower bud with a strong, warm and slightly numbing spice flavour. Used in spiced syrups, mulled drinks and hot toddies, often studded into citrus.

name: Star Anise
description: Star-shaped dried seed pod with a sweet liquorice flavour. Floated whole as a garnish or simmered into spiced syrups and mulled drinks.

name: Anise
description: Small grey-green seed, also called aniseed, with a sweet liquorice flavour. The key botanical in pastis, ouzo and absinthe, used in syrups and tinctures.

name: Cardamom
description: Small green pods holding black seeds with a citrusy, floral and eucalyptus-like spice. Crushed into syrups, bitters and infusions.

name: Black Cardamom
description: Large dark brown cardamom pod dried over open fire, giving a smoky, camphor-like flavour. Used in savoury syrups, tinctures and infusions.

name: Vanilla
description: Cured seed pod of the vanilla orchid, with a sweet, creamy and floral aroma. Split and steeped into syrups, spirits and creams.

name: Vanilla Extract
description: Concentrated liquid made by steeping vanilla pods in alcohol. A few drops add vanilla flavour to syrups, creams and flips without needing whole pods.

name: Black Pepper
description: Dried peppercorns with a sharp, woody heat. Cracked fresh over savoury drinks, or steeped into syrups and tinctures to add a dry, spicy bite.

name: Pink Peppercorn
description: Dried pink berries of the pepper tree, fruity and lightly peppery with a resinous sweetness. Used in syrups and as a crushed garnish.

name: Sichuan Pepper
description: Dried husks of the prickly ash berry, with a citrus aroma and a tingling, numbing effect on the tongue. Used in tinctures, syrups and salt rims.

name: Allspice
description: Dried berry of the pimento tree from Jamaica, tasting like clove, cinnamon and nutmeg together. The flavour of pimento dram and many tiki syrups.

name: Ginger
description: Knobbly fresh root with a hot, peppery and citrusy flavour. Juiced, muddled or cooked into syrup for Mules, Penicillins and ginger beer.

name: Turmeric
description: Bright orange root, used fresh or as a dried powder, with an earthy, bitter and peppery flavour. Adds a strong yellow colour to syrups and juices.

name: Chilli
description: Fresh or dried hot pepper, ranging from mild to very hot. Muddled, sliced or infused into spirits and syrups to add heat, as in a Spicy Margarita.

name: Jalapeño
description: Medium-hot green Mexican chilli with a fresh, grassy flavour. Sliced into shakers or infused into tequila for Spicy Margaritas, and used as a garnish.

name: Habanero
description: Very hot, lantern-shaped chilli with a fruity, apricot-like aroma. Used carefully in tinctures, shrubs and infusions where a little goes a long way.

name: Bird's Eye Chilli
description: Small, thin and very hot chilli used across Southeast Asia. Sliced or bruised into shaken drinks, or infused into spirits and syrups for sharp heat.

name: Saffron
description: Dried red stigmas of the saffron crocus, with a honeyed, hay-like aroma and a strong golden colour. Steeped into syrups, gin and tinctures.

name: Tonka Bean
description: Wrinkled black seed from South America with an aroma of vanilla, almond and cherry. Grated sparingly over drinks or steeped into syrups and spirits.

name: Cacao
description: Seeds of the cacao tree, fermented and dried as the raw material for chocolate. Used as beans, nibs or husks to give a bitter chocolate flavour.

name: Cacao Nibs
description: Crushed pieces of roasted cacao beans, bitter and nutty with no added sugar. Infused into spirits, vermouth and syrups for a dry chocolate note.

name: Coffee Beans
description: Roasted seeds of the coffee plant. Ground for brewing, infused into spirits, or floated in threes as the classic Espresso Martini garnish.

name: Juniper Berries
description: Small blue-black cones of the juniper shrub with a piney, resinous flavour. The defining botanical of gin, also used in syrups and as a garnish.

name: Coriander Seed
description: Dried round seed of the coriander plant, with a warm, citrusy and lightly spicy flavour. A core gin botanical, used in syrups, bitters and tinctures.

name: Fennel Seed
description: Small green-brown seed with a sweet anise flavour. Toasted and steeped into syrups, tinctures and infusions for a gentle liquorice note.

name: Wattleseed
description: Roasted and ground seeds of Australian acacia trees, with a coffee, chocolate and hazelnut flavour. Used in syrups, infusions and cream drinks.

name: Sarsaparilla
description: Dried root of a tropical vine with an earthy, vanilla and wintergreen flavour. The traditional base of root beer style syrups and sodas.

name: Sandalwood
description: Fragrant heartwood with a creamy, warm and woody scent. Food-grade chips or powder are used in tinctures, syrups and as an aromatic smoke.

name: Palo Santo
description: Aromatic South American wood with a sweet, resinous scent of pine, mint and citrus. Burned to smoke a glass or steeped into tinctures and syrups.

name: Sugar
description: Crystallised sucrose from sugar cane or sugar beet. Dissolved into syrups, muddled in the glass, or used on rims. The basic sweetener behind the bar.

name: White Sugar
description: Refined white granulated sugar with a clean, neutral sweetness. The standard choice for simple syrup, cordials and sherbets.

name: Caster Sugar
description: Finely ground white sugar, called superfine sugar in the US. It dissolves quickly, so it suits syrups, oleo saccharum and stirring straight into drinks.

name: Demerara Sugar
description: Coarse, golden-brown cane sugar with a light toffee flavour. Made into rich demerara syrup for Old Fashioneds, rum drinks and tiki recipes.

name: Brown Sugar
description: Soft, moist sugar coloured and flavoured with molasses, light or dark. Gives syrups a caramel and toffee note and is used in hot and coffee drinks.

name: Muscovado Sugar
description: Unrefined dark cane sugar with a high molasses content, sticky and rich with treacle and liquorice notes. Used for deep, dark syrups.

name: Icing Sugar
description: White sugar ground to a fine powder, called powdered or confectioners' sugar in the US. Dusted over mint and fruit garnishes on juleps and cobblers.

name: Raw Sugar
description: Lightly refined cane sugar with large golden crystals, also sold as turbinado. It keeps some molasses flavour and makes a richer tasting syrup.

name: Palm Sugar
description: Sugar made from the boiled sap of palm trees, sold in blocks or discs. Gula melaka from coconut palm has a smoky, butterscotch and caramel flavour.

name: Fructose
description: Fruit sugar sold as a fine white powder, noticeably sweeter than table sugar. Used in measured amounts to sweeten and balance cordials and batched drinks.

name: Sugar Cube
description: Small pressed cube of white sugar, roughly one teaspoon. Soaked with bitters and muddled for an Old Fashioned, Sazerac or Champagne Cocktail.

name: Brown Sugar Cube
description: Rough pressed cube of demerara or brown cane sugar. Used like a white sugar cube in Old Fashioneds and Champagne Cocktails for a richer taste.

name: Honey
description: Thick, sweet syrup made by bees from flower nectar, with flavour that varies by blossom. Usually thinned with water into honey syrup for mixing.

name: Agave Syrup
description: Sweetener made from the sap of the agave plant, thinner than honey and sweeter than sugar. The usual sweetener in a Tommy's Margarita.

name: Maple Syrup
description: Syrup boiled down from the sap of sugar maple trees, mainly in Canada and the northeastern US. Woody and caramel-like, good with whiskey and rum.

name: Molasses
description: Thick, dark syrup left over from refining sugar cane, bittersweet with a burnt, mineral edge. Blackstrap is the darkest grade. Used in small amounts.

name: Date Syrup
description: Dark, thick syrup made from cooked and pressed dates, with a caramel and dried fruit flavour. Used as a sweetener in stirred and coffee drinks.

name: Golden Syrup
description: Thick amber syrup made from refined cane sugar, a staple in British and Australian kitchens. It has a buttery, light caramel flavour.

name: Dulce de Leche
description: Thick Latin American caramel made by slowly cooking milk and sugar. Shaken into creamy dessert drinks or thinned into a syrup.

name: Cream of Coconut
description: Thick, sweetened coconut cream sold in tins or squeeze bottles. It is the coconut part of a Piña Colada, and is not the same as coconut cream.

name: Egg
description: Whole chicken egg, used raw in flips and eggnog for a rich, custardy texture. Freshness matters, and the white and yolk are often used separately.

name: Egg White
description: The clear white of a chicken egg, shaken into sours and fizzes to give a silky texture and a stable foam. It adds body without adding flavour.

name: Egg Yolk
description: The yellow centre of a chicken egg, rich in fat. Shaken into flips, golden fizzes and eggnog for a thick, custard-like texture.

name: Aquafaba
description: The cooking liquid from chickpeas, usually poured from a tin. It foams like egg white when shaken, which makes it the common vegan option for sours.

name: Milk
description: Fresh cow's milk, normally full fat behind the bar. Used in milk punches, White Russians and coffee drinks, and curdled to clarify punches.

name: Cream
description: The fat-rich layer of cow's milk, sold as single, pouring or whipping cream. Shaken into Alexanders and Grasshoppers or floated on Irish Coffee.

name: Double Cream
description: Thick cream with a high fat content, known as heavy cream in the US. Whips easily and floats well, as on an Irish Coffee or Ramos Gin Fizz.

name: Half and Half
description: American dairy product made of equal parts whole milk and light cream, around 12 percent fat. Used in White Russians, Ramos Gin Fizzes and coffee drinks.

name: Butter
description: Churned dairy fat, usually unsalted for bar use. Melted for Hot Buttered Rum, browned for a nutty flavour, or used to fat wash spirits.

name: Ghee
description: Clarified butter from South Asia, cooked until the milk solids brown and are strained out. Its nutty flavour and pure fat make it handy for fat washing.

name: Coconut Milk
description: Milky liquid pressed from grated coconut flesh and water, unsweetened and sold in tins. Used in creamy tropical drinks and for milk punch clarification.

name: Coconut Cream
description: Thick, unsweetened cream pressed from coconut flesh, richer and higher in fat than coconut milk. Gives body to Piña Coladas and dairy-free drinks.

name: Oat Milk
description: Plant-based milk made from oats and water, with a mild cereal sweetness. Barista versions foam well and stand in for dairy in coffee and cream drinks.

name: Almond Milk
description: Plant-based milk made from ground almonds and water, light with a gentle nutty taste. Used as a dairy-free option in creamy and coffee drinks.

name: Soy Milk
description: Plant-based milk made from soaked and ground soybeans, with a creamy texture and a mild bean flavour. Used in dairy-free cream drinks and milk punches.

name: Rice Milk
description: Thin plant-based milk made from milled rice and water, naturally sweet and neutral in taste. Used in horchata style drinks and dairy-free recipes.

name: Yoghurt
description: Milk fermented with live cultures until thick and tangy. Shaken into lassi style drinks, used for milk washing, or strained for its acidic whey.

name: Condensed Milk
description: Milk cooked down with sugar into a thick, very sweet syrup, sold in tins. Used in Batidas, Vietnamese coffee drinks and creamy dessert serves.

name: Ice Cream
description: Frozen dessert of churned cream, milk and sugar, most often vanilla behind the bar. Blended into boozy shakes or scooped into floats and affogatos.

name: Olive Oil
description: Oil pressed from olives, grassy and peppery when extra virgin. Dropped on the surface of Martinis and sours, or used to fat wash gin and vodka.

name: Sesame Oil
description: Oil pressed from sesame seeds, with a deep nutty aroma when made from toasted seeds. Used for fat washing whisky and rum or as a few aromatic drops.

name: Coconut Oil
description: Fat pressed from coconut flesh, solid at room temperature. Virgin oil tastes of coconut and refined oil is odourless. A common choice for fat washing.

name: Cocoa Butter
description: Pale yellow fat pressed from cacao beans, with a mild chocolate aroma. Melted and used to fat wash spirits for a smooth, white chocolate note.

name: Citric Acid
description: White powdered acid that gives lemons and limes their sourness. Dissolved in water to acidify cordials and juices or to make shelf-stable sour mixes.

name: Malic Acid
description: White powdered acid found in apples and stone fruit, with a rounded, lingering sourness. Often blended with citric acid to mimic lime juice.

name: Tartaric Acid
description: Powdered acid found in grapes, with a sharp, dry and wine-like sourness. Used to adjust cordials and to build grape or wine style acidity.

name: Lactic Acid
description: Mild acid from fermentation, sold as a liquid or powder, with the soft, creamy tang of yoghurt. Adds roundness to cordials and stirred drinks.

name: Ascorbic Acid
description: Vitamin C in white powder form. Bars add a small pinch to fresh juices and cordials to slow browning and keep colours bright. It has a light tartness.

name: Acid Phosphate
description: Solution of phosphoric acid and mineral salts from the old soda fountain era. Adds dry, clean sourness with no fruit flavour to sodas and cocktails.

name: Salt
description: Sodium chloride in crystal form. A pinch or a few drops of saline rounds out bitterness and lifts flavour, and coarse salt is used for glass rims.

name: Sea Salt
description: Salt made by evaporating seawater, sold as fine grains or flakes. Flaky sea salt is the usual choice for Margarita rims and for saline solution.

name: Table Salt
description: Fine-grained refined salt, often with added iodine and anti-caking agent. It dissolves fast, so it is used for saline solution and seasoning batches.

name: Kosher Salt
description: Coarse, flaky salt with no additives, the standard cooking salt in the US. Used for salt rims and for making saline solution by weight.

name: Celery Salt
description: Seasoning made of salt mixed with ground celery seed. A standard part of a Bloody Mary, in the mix or on the rim of the glass.

name: MSG
description: Monosodium glutamate, a white crystalline seasoning that adds savoury umami taste. Used in tiny amounts, often dissolved in saline, in savoury drinks.

name: Xanthan Gum
description: Fine powder made by fermentation and used as a thickener and stabiliser. A very small amount adds body to syrups and keeps blended drinks from splitting.

name: Gum Arabic
description: Dried sap of the acacia tree, sold as powder or crystals. Dissolved into gomme syrup to give stirred drinks a silky, weightier mouthfeel.

name: Agar
description: Setting agent made from red seaweed, sold as powder or flakes. Bars use it to clarify juices by setting and straining, and to make firm jellies.

name: Gelatine
description: Setting agent made from animal collagen, sold as leaves or powder. Used for jellies and foams and for freeze and thaw clarification of juices.

name: Pectinase
description: Enzyme that breaks down pectin in fruit, best known by the brand name Pectinex. A few drops help juices and purées clarify and separate cleanly.

name: Soy Lecithin
description: Emulsifier extracted from soybeans, sold as powder or granules. Blended into a flavoured liquid to whip up light, stable airs for topping drinks.

name: Methylcellulose
description: Plant-derived powder that thickens and foams liquids. Used with other gums as a vegan foaming agent in place of egg white in sours.

name: Glycerine
description: Clear, thick and slightly sweet food-grade liquid, also spelled glycerin. Added in small amounts to give body, or used as a base for alcohol-free tinctures.

name: Activated Charcoal
description: Fine black food-grade powder made from charred coconut shell or wood. A pinch turns a drink jet black and adds almost no flavour.

name: Matcha
description: Finely ground powder of shade-grown Japanese green tea leaves. Whisked or shaken into drinks for a grassy, savoury and slightly bitter flavour and green colour.

name: Cocoa Powder
description: Unsweetened powder ground from roasted cacao after most of the fat is pressed out. Dusted over creamy drinks or cooked into chocolate syrup.

name: Carob Powder
description: Powder ground from the roasted pods of the carob tree, sweet with a mild cocoa and caramel flavour. Used in syrups and as a dusted garnish.

name: Coffee
description: Drink brewed from roasted, ground coffee beans, bitter and aromatic. Used hot in Irish Coffee or chilled in highballs, and as a base for coffee syrups.

name: Espresso
description: Concentrated coffee made by forcing hot water through finely ground beans under pressure. A fresh shot gives the Espresso Martini its flavour and foam.

name: Cold Brew Coffee
description: Coffee steeped in cold water for 12 to 24 hours, giving a smooth, low-acid and less bitter brew. Often made as a concentrate for cocktails.

name: Filter Coffee
description: Coffee brewed by pouring hot water through ground beans in a paper or metal filter. Lighter than espresso and the usual base for an Irish Coffee.

name: Tea
description: Drink made by steeping the dried leaves of the tea plant in water. Used hot or cold in punches and highballs, and infused into spirits and syrups.

name: Black Tea
description: Fully oxidised tea with a dark colour and a brisk, malty and tannic flavour. The classic tea for punches, iced tea and tea infused spirits.

name: Earl Grey Tea
description: Black tea scented with oil of bergamot, giving a floral citrus aroma. Infused into gin for the Earl Grey MarTEAni and cooked into syrups.

name: Green Tea
description: Unoxidised tea with a pale colour and a fresh, grassy and lightly bitter flavour. Brewed cool for highballs, punches, syrups and infusions.

name: Sencha
description: Everyday Japanese green tea made from steamed whole leaves, with a fresh, grassy and slightly savoury taste. Cold brewed for highballs and cordials.

name: Hojicha
description: Japanese green tea roasted over charcoal until brown, with a toasty, nutty and caramel flavour and little bitterness. Used in syrups and infusions.

name: Oolong Tea
description: Partly oxidised Chinese and Taiwanese tea that sits between green and black tea. Flavours run from floral and creamy to roasted and fruity.

name: Jasmine Tea
description: Green tea scented with jasmine blossoms, giving a sweet floral aroma over a light tea base. Cold brewed or infused into gin, vodka and syrups.

name: Chamomile Tea
description: Caffeine-free herbal tea brewed from dried chamomile flowers, with an apple and honey flavour. Used in hot drinks, syrups and whisky infusions.

name: Hibiscus Tea
description: Deep red herbal tea brewed from dried hibiscus calyces, tart and cranberry-like. Served cold as agua de Jamaica and used for colour and acidity.

name: Lapsang Souchong
description: Chinese black tea dried over pine wood fires, with a strong smoky, tarry aroma. Infused into spirits and syrups to add smoke without peat.

name: Chai
description: Indian spiced tea, a blend of black tea with cardamom, cinnamon, ginger, clove and pepper. Brewed strong for syrups, milk punches and hot drinks.

name: Rooibos
description: Caffeine-free red herbal tea from a South African shrub, with a sweet, nutty and vanilla-like flavour. Steeped for syrups and spirit infusions.

name: Water
description: Plain still water. Used to dilute batched and bottled cocktails, to make syrups and teas, and to lengthen spirits such as whisky.

name: Filtered Water
description: Tap water passed through a filter to remove chlorine and off flavours. The standard water for dilution in batches, syrups, cordials and clear ice.

name: Hot Water
description: Water heated to just off the boil. Used to build Hot Toddies and other hot drinks, to brew teas, and to dissolve honey and sugar into syrups.

name: Orange Flower Water
description: Fragrant water distilled from bitter orange blossoms. A few drops perfume a Ramos Gin Fizz and it is a traditional part of orgeat syrup.

name: Rose Water
description: Fragrant water distilled from rose petals, widely used in Middle Eastern and South Asian cooking. A few drops add a strong floral scent.

name: Olive
description: Brined fruit of the olive tree, green or black, salty and savoury. The classic Martini garnish, served on a pick, plain or stuffed.

name: Castelvetrano Olive
description: Bright green Sicilian olive from the Nocellara del Belice variety, with firm flesh and a mild, buttery taste. A popular Martini garnish.

name: Gordal Olive
description: Very large, meaty green olive from Andalusia in Spain, with a mild flavour and firm bite. Served whole on a pick in Martinis and Gildas.

name: Kalamata Olive
description: Dark purple, almond-shaped Greek olive cured in brine and wine vinegar. Rich and fruity, used as a garnish and in savoury infusions.

name: Olive Brine
description: The salty, savoury liquid that jarred olives are packed in. A measure of it is what turns a Martini into a Dirty Martini.

name: Cocktail Onion
description: Small pearl onion pickled in a lightly sweet vinegar brine. It is the garnish that defines a Gibson, and the brine can season the drink too.

name: Pickle
description: Small cucumber pickled in vinegar or salt brine, such as a gherkin or cornichon. Used as a savoury garnish for Martinis and Bloody Marys.

name: Pickle Brine
description: The sour, salty liquid from a jar of pickled cucumbers, often flavoured with dill and garlic. Poured as a Pickleback chaser or in savoury Martinis.

name: Caper
description: Pickled flower bud of the caper bush, sharp, salty and floral. Used as a savoury garnish or with its brine in Martinis and tomato drinks.

name: Celery
description: Crisp green stalk vegetable with a fresh, salty and slightly bitter taste. A leafy stalk is the classic Bloody Mary garnish, and the juice suits gin.

name: Horseradish
description: Pungent white root with a sharp, sinus-clearing heat. Freshly grated or from a jar, it gives a Bloody Mary its bite.

name: Beetroot
description: Deep purple root vegetable with a sweet, earthy flavour. Juiced, roasted or pickled, and used for its colour in shrubs, cordials and infusions.

name: Carrot
description: Orange root vegetable with a sweet, earthy flavour. Juiced for savoury and brunch drinks or cooked into cordials and shrubs.

name: Capsicum
description: Sweet pepper with no heat, called bell pepper in the US, in red, yellow or green. Juiced or muddled for a fresh, vegetal note with tequila or gin.

name: Wasabi
description: Japanese green root grated into a paste with a sharp, nose-tingling heat that fades fast. Most tubes and powders are horseradish based.

name: Miso
description: Japanese paste of fermented soybeans, salt and koji, salty and rich in umami. Blended into syrups and caramels to add savoury depth.

name: White Miso
description: Pale, short-fermented miso, also called shiro miso, with a mild, sweet and gently salty taste. The usual miso for syrups, caramels and fat washes.

name: Soy Sauce
description: Dark, salty sauce brewed from fermented soybeans and wheat. A few drops add umami and salt to savoury drinks, Bloody Marys and caramel syrups.

name: Fish Sauce
description: Thin amber sauce from Southeast Asia made of fermented anchovies and salt. Used by the drop for a salty, savoury kick in Bloody Marys and Micheladas.

name: Sesame
description: Small oil-rich seeds with a nutty flavour that deepens when toasted. Used for orgeat style syrups, infusions and as a rim or garnish.

name: Black Sesame
description: Unhulled black variety of sesame seed, with a stronger, earthier and slightly bitter nutty taste. Used in syrups, pastes and as a dark rim.

name: Black Garlic
description: Garlic aged with gentle heat for weeks until the cloves turn black, soft and sweet. Tastes of balsamic, molasses and tamarind and is used in syrups.

name: Mushroom
description: Edible fungi with an earthy, savoury flavour. Fresh or dried mushrooms are infused into spirits and syrups to add umami and forest floor notes.

name: Shiitake
description: East Asian mushroom with a brown cap and a meaty, smoky flavour, sold fresh or dried. Dried shiitake is steeped into spirits and syrups for umami.

name: Sweet Potato
description: Starchy root vegetable with orange, white or purple flesh and an earthy sweetness. Roasted and made into syrups, purées and infusions.

name: Seaweed
description: Edible marine algae such as nori, kombu, wakame and dulse. Adds a salty, mineral and umami note to infusions, tinctures and garnishes.

name: Nori
description: Japanese seaweed pressed and dried into thin, dark green sheets. Toasted and cut into strips for a savoury garnish, or infused into spirits.

name: Kombu
description: Thick dried kelp from Japan that is the base of dashi stock. Steeped into spirits, vermouth and syrups for a clean, salty umami depth.

name: Caviar
description: Salt-cured roe of sturgeon, with a briny, buttery taste. Served as a luxury garnish or side bite with Martinis and Champagne drinks.

name: Dehydrated Citrus Wheel
description: Thin slice of lemon, lime, orange or grapefruit dried until crisp. A long-lasting garnish that floats on the drink or clips to the rim.

name: Edible Flower
description: Food-safe fresh blossoms such as viola, pansy, cornflower, nasturtium and orchid. Placed on foam or ice as a colourful garnish with little flavour.

name: Pineapple Frond
description: A spiky green leaf pulled from the crown of a pineapple. Used singly or in a fan as an upright garnish on tiki and tropical drinks.

name: Candied Ginger
description: Pieces of ginger root cooked in sugar syrup and rolled in sugar, chewy, sweet and hot. Skewered as the garnish on a Penicillin or Mule.

name: Chocolate
description: Solid confection made from cacao, sugar and often milk. Grated or shaved over creamy drinks, melted into syrups, or served on the side.

name: Dark Chocolate
description: Chocolate with a high share of cacao and little or no milk, bittersweet and intense. Grated over drinks or melted into rich syrups and ganache.

name: White Chocolate
description: Sweet, creamy confection made from cocoa butter, sugar and milk with no cocoa solids. Melted into syrups and creams or grated as a garnish.
